setting: The story is set at a company in present-day Seoul. Desks, meeting rooms, the pantry, the fifteen seconds inside a lift and the after-work dinner nobody actually wants to attend are the texture of an ordinary day. The constraints here are written down: policy, reporting lines, the year-end review. Romance is not forbidden, but the moment it appears on any form it stops being a matter between two people - and nothing in a company goes unwritten for long.

statNotes.selfId: Rises when she says what she actually thinks in a room where the safe answer was available - a review, a client meeting, a decision that is already half made. Falls when she says the safe thing instead.
statNotes.secrecy: Falls when the relationship becomes legible to anyone in the building - a colleague on the same floor, a shared calendar, a card swipe at an odd hour, a form that asks. Rises when an ordinary work reason holds.
statNotes.mood: Driven by workload, deadlines and where the quarter is, and by how the last exchange with the target member ended.

identities.name: Colleague
identities.background: [Identity: Colleague] You and {name} are on the same team at the same level, with one partition between your desks. Typical events: The same project keeps you both up rewriting a deck, on your third coffee from the convenience store by dawn; She takes the blame for something that was going to land on you; The company dinner breaks up and your routes home overlap, so you walk a long way; The year-end rankings come out and your names are next to each other. Advantage: Same level, same team - being together needs no reason at all. Disadvantage: And for exactly that reason the whole team is in one field of view, and any change is seen by the same people.

identities.name: Team lead
identities.background: [Identity: Team Lead] You lead this team and {name} reports to you. Typical events: You keep the hardest client for yourself rather than assigning her to it; Ten minutes of a twenty-minute one-to-one are not about work; Her proposal comes back rejected from above and you tell the room it was your call; Year-end forces you to rank the whole team, and you know how long you hesitated. Advantage: You decide what she works on, with whom, and for how long - which is the closest thing to looking after someone this building has. Disadvantage: You also decide her review, so anything she says to you might not be the thing she wanted to say.

identities.name: Direct report
identities.background: [Identity: Direct Report] {name} is your team lead and you report to her directly. Typical events: What you hand in comes back unrecognisable, with a line saying you will be able to do this yourself next time; She pulls you out of a meeting that was never going to reach a decision; You are still there late and the light over her desk is still on too; At your review she scores you higher than you expected and you do not dare ask why. Advantage: You have a reason to speak every day, and it is the most private kind of reason. Disadvantage: You cannot tell how much of her care is the job, and she cannot tell how much of your effort is something else.

workTitle.because: reports to them and every member sits above her on the org chart

identities.name: New hire
identities.background: [Identity: New Hire] You are the newest person on this team, and everyone here is your senior. Typical events: In your first week you book the meeting room for the wrong hour and she is the one who apologises; She shares her entire folder of templates with you; Someone keeps refilling your glass at the company dinner and she moves it out of reach; On the last day of your probation she says only that you should stay. Advantage: Asking a senior for help is the most natural way to get close, and nobody finds it strange. Disadvantage: You have no standing yet - her looking after you is her job, and anything you read into it is your problem.

workTitle.because: is the newest hire and every member joined before her

identities.name: Contractor
identities.background: [Identity: Contractor] You do not work for this company. You are the contact from a vendor, a consultancy or an outsourced team: you have a door pass and no employee number. Typical events: There is no chair for you at their meeting, so you stand beside the projector; At the end-of-project dinner someone asks which side you are on; She stops you in the lift and what she asks about is not work; A week before the contract ends, neither of you has mentioned the next one. Advantage: You are on nobody's reporting line, so the company's policy does not reach the two of you. Disadvantage: And for exactly that reason you can disappear at any time - when the contract ends it ends, and nobody owes you an explanation.

identities.name: HR
identities.background: [Identity: HR] You work in HR. Onboarding, reviews, complaints, resignations - every document about these people passes through you in the end. Typical events: You processed her joining file and you remember every line of it; Someone comes to complain about her team and you have to hear both sides out; The company issues a new policy on relationships between employees and you are the one who drafted it; She comes to ask you something on behalf of a friend and you both know that is not true. Advantage: You know better than anyone in this building who is what to whom - you wrote the rules. Disadvantage: You wrote the rules, so you also know better than anyone that if this is found, you are the first one who gets handled.

identities.name: Main Member's Ex-Girlfriend
identities.background:
[Special Identity: Main Member's Ex-Girlfriend]
- You and {name} were lovers, breaking up years ago due to {reason}
- You still keep {keepsake} to this day
- Now a reorganisation has put the two of you on the same team: awkwardness, complicated feelings, things left unsaid. Early interactions involve deliberate distance, averted eyes, polite but distant
- Other colleagues may or may not know about your past. As the game progresses, you may reconcile or go your separate ways

keepsake: a photo of you both behind an ID badge
a sticky note she put on your monitor
the receipt from the night you both worked late

modes.free: [Story Mode: Free] No authored plot events - the relationship itself is the plot. Affection grows slowly. Focus on details and subtle tension: the same desk, the same lift, the same walk to the station. No rushing into relationship.
modes.romance: [Story Mode: Romance] Ambiguous & Romantic. Natural progression with mutual attraction. Members flirt during Flirting stage.
modes.pressure: [Story Mode: Pressure] Workplace scrutiny and policy exposure higher, secrecy changes doubled. Being seen together carries weight: a shared calendar, a colleague on the same floor, and a written policy that has a name for this.
modes.dramatic: [Story Mode: Dramatic] Light comedic. Love triangle scenes probability doubled. Members compete more openly for your attention.

phases.line: - Phase 1 (Rounds 1-6): First encounters. Handovers and corridors, professional politeness, subtle curiosity. No romantic moves.
- Phase 2 (Rounds 7-14): Repeated encounters. Growing familiarity, work that runs late, accidental touches, first hints of jealousy.
- Phase 3 (Rounds 15-24): Reality pressure. Talk on the floor, a policy that has a name for this, a reorganisation, career against feelings.
- Phase 4 (Rounds 25+): Consequences. Established relationship, exposure risk, possible proposal or separation.

places.name: Open-plan floor
places.desc: The partitions stop at shoulder height; everyone sees who walks past whose desk.

places.name: Meeting room
places.desc: Glass walls, and lowering the blind draws more attention than leaving it up.

places.name: Pantry
places.desc: The six square metres the whole company's news moves through fastest.

places.name: Lift
places.desc: Fifteen seconds. Anything can be said before the doors open and nothing after.

places.name: Rooftop
places.desc: The only place with no camera on it, and the coldest place in the building.

places.name: Company dinner
places.desc: Smoke off the grill, a glass being refilled, and a whole table watching the two of you.

places.name: Fire stairs
places.desc: Nobody takes the stairs, so nothing said here is overheard.

places.name: Archive room
places.desc: The light has to be switched on by hand, and the door locks from the inside.

places.name: Late-night taxi
places.desc: The back seat, street lights going past one at a time, the driver listening to the radio.

places.name: Convenience store downstairs
places.desc: Two in the morning, steam off the hot case, and the clerk does not look up.

scenario: A night that ran until there were two of you left. Only your row of lights is still on across the whole floor and the air conditioning stopped hours ago. You were both only waiting on the same document, and neither of you left first.

castLife.theirs: deadlines, client meetings, the quarterly numbers, this company
castLife.notHers: no meeting here to be late for and no line on their org chart
castLife.recentBeat: the meeting she just walked out of
